label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl, models/w_longjump.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, B, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is a 55-gallon drum: a straight-sided cylinder with a flat lid, a bung standing up from the top, and rolling hoops near the top and bottom. The front, side, back and four angled views all show the same shape, with no part missing or sticking out where the brief does not ask for one.

M2.reason: The measured size is 24.2 x 23.6 x 36.7 units. The brief asks for 23 across and 34 high, so the width is 5% over, the depth 2.6% over, and the height 7.9% over. Each is within the 15% band for a brief's size.

M3.reason: The brief names a drum and a hazard stripe. The drum is there with its rolling hoops (the bands at the top and bottom), its bung on the lid, and a full band of yellow and black diagonal hazard stripe at mid-height. The stripe is painted on, which counts as present. No line-up model of the drum's kind is in the picture to add other required parts.

M4.reason: The steel body is grey-blue with mottled patches, which reads as weathered, rusted steel in the game's palette. The hazard band is yellow and black as the brief asks. The rust is subtle: it shows as grey mottling rather than strong orange-brown, so this is the weakest point, but it is not clearly off.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe sits in one band at mid-height in every side view, with sharp diagonal yellow and black bars. The rolling hoops are shaded with a worn edge and the body has a wear mottle. These are the surface details the brief asks for, in their places.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by rule. In the four-model line-up, the drum (B) sits beside three of Half-Life's own and looks like one of the game's props in scale and finish. The separate line-up test is what decides M6 here.

M7.reason: A drum has no front, and the model stands upright on its base at the origin, with its bung on top. Each side view is correctly oriented and the model sits flat on its bottom rim.

M8.reason: The model passes SMAK's check with no errors. It has 372 triangles, which is over twice the 99-triangle median of Half-Life's own props of its kind, but under the 422 the most of Valve's own spends on that kind and size, so it passes the amended bar. The base and lid are closed, and nothing floats or is inside out.
